newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Savage sees steady U.S. zinc premiums.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Savage sees steady U.S. zinc premiums.

text.p: Zinc producer premiums in the United States of around 5.5 cents a pound will carry over into 1997, Savage Zinc Inc of Tenessee said here on Thursday.
"We are anticipating the same pricing structure in 1997 as in 1996," David Rice, president of Savage Zinc told a news briefing.
Rice said the premiums had remained constant at between five and six cents a pound throughout 1996 so far.
Savage zinc is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Australia-based Savage Resources Ltd.
Premiums reflect margins the metal commands above an average monthly London Metal Exchange price and thus were largely immune to fluctuations in the zinc price, Rice said.
Rice said he saw an improving outlook for zinc, although not to the degree as some others in the market.

He said speculation in the market that the former long zinc position of Spanish zinc group Asturiana de Zinc's may have been liquidated of transferred to the control of financier George Soros could indicate a firmer market to come.
However, Rice remained conservative in his outlook.
Some recent forecasts for increase in zinc prices appeared "overly enthusiastic" in the short term, he said.
"They expect (US) 70 cents (a pound)... that would be heaven," Rice said.
Benchmark LME three-month zinc fetches about US$0.48 a pound.
Rice said zinc was poised to respond to declining LME stocks and a forecast supply defict of around 150,000 tonnes this year

Rice said Savage continued to "toy with the idea" of lifting capacity at its Clarksville, Tenn, zinc refinery to around 180,000 tonnes a year from the current 105,000 tonnes, but added there were no firm plans to do so.
Environmental permitting enabling the refinery to expand were likely to be granted in 1997.
The refinery produces about one-third of the U.S. ouptut of zinc and supplies around eight percent of U.S. demand annually, Rice said.
Each one U.S. cent move in the zinc price means about A$2.2 million to Savage's bottom line, Savage Resources' managing director Jim Wall said.
